huntingHours.detail: A THIRD KIND OF HOURS RULE, AND THE INVERSE OF WASHINGTON'S. Not a table dressed as a formula but a TERM WITH NO FORMULA AT ALL. r. 220-2-.05: "Legal hunting hours for game birds during the open season shall be daylight hours only, except as otherwise provided by law or regulation." "Daylight hours" is UNDEFINED in the rule, so North Ground's astronomy cannot reproduce it — there is no numeric rule to reproduce, and choosing an offset would be inventing the law. Kentucky states the identical phrase and DEFINES it in KRS 150.010(8), which is why the same words are certifiable in one state and not the other; carrying Kentucky's definition into Alabama would be exactly the error §8 forbids. The basis is recorded as AUTHORITY_TABLE because, as with Washington, whatever fixes the window is the authority's and not ours — the difference is that Alabama has not published one. Alabama then layers computable solar offsets and fixed civil clock times onto specific species and geographies, which are not yet read.

Five Iowa species state affirmatively that there are no hours restrictions, in the codified rules AND independently in the booklet's SHOOTING HOURS column printing "No Restrictions". Encoding half-an-hour-before-sunrise for them would invent a restriction the authority does not impose, which §8 treats as seriously as inventing a permission. Iowa also has genuine FIXED CIVIL CLOCK rules (pheasant, partridge and quail at 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.) and a species whose offset differs BY LICENCE TYPE. The statute was checked too: Iowa Code ch. 481A and ch. 483A contain NO statutory hunting-hours provision, with a positive control run for that absence. No zone-specific or longitude-specific time provision appears anywhere in IAC 571, so Iowa presents no Atikokan-style split — though that all of Iowa observes a single civil zone was not independently verified from a primary source, and must be before the 8 a.m. rules are rendered as local clock times.

huntingHours.detail: A DEFINED TERM, AND SEARCHING FOR THE TIMES PRODUCES A FALSE ABSENCE. Kentucky's species regulations mostly state no times at all — they prohibit taking outside "daylight hours" — and KRS 150.010(8) defines that once for the whole chapter. A first pass searching 301 KAR 2:172 for "sunrise" found nothing and nearly recorded deer as having no hours rule. The rule is there, by defined term. Positive control on the statute: it is "150.010 Definitions for chapter" with 46 defined terms. No published table exists: across the 40-page guide (153,696 characters extracted) "sunrise/sunset table", "table of sunrise" and "appendix" each return 0 hits, with a positive control on the same text finding "shooting hours" 10 times, "telecheck" 41 and "hunter orange" 33 — so the zero is a true zero. Kentucky's astronomy is therefore reproducible, unlike Washington's or Pennsylvania's. One presentation caveat: Kentucky counties are split between Eastern and Central time, and Ky_County_Polygons_WM carries no time-zone field, so the displayed clock needs that mapping from elsewhere.

Three things follow. (1) It is not a point solar calculation, so the AUTHORITY_TABLE basis is the correct one. (2) It is temporal in the strongest sense: § 141.4 was amended 29 May 2026, effective 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027, 56 Pa.B. 3128, so the rule is re-enacted annually and must be evaluated against the hunt date rather than cached. (3) Its codified exceptions are not adjustments to one window but different windows: furbearers — raccoon, fox, skunk, opossum, coyote, bobcat, weasel — may be hunted ANY HOUR, DAY OR NIGHT; spring turkey runs to 12 noon until the third Saturday and to half an hour after sunset thereafter; migratory birds close AT SUNSET except in the snow goose conservation and September resident goose seasons. Also unresolved and recorded in the map findings: the meridian-band layer itself has 7 bands on the Commission's ArcGIS Online account and 6 on its own server.

huntingHours.detail: WASHINGTON IS NOT A SOLAR-FORMULA STATE, and it reads like one. WAC 220-416-020(1) says "The following tables show the lawful hunting hours (1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset)" — the parenthetical states how the tables were BUILT; the tables are the rule. There are SEVEN of them, subsections (3) to (9), selected by the weekday 1 September falls on; each splits into Western and Eastern Washington with its own A.M. and P.M. columns; rows are week-long date bands; the table is explicitly partitioned into a daylight-saving block and a Pacific-standard block with one transition row; times are wall-clock rounded to five minutes. The rule is certified and cited. No exact clock is offered because the rows have not been transcribed, and computing one from the parenthetical would return times that disagree with the printed ones — which are the law. The AUTHORITY_TABLE basis exists to hold them when they are read.
